The executable performs no legitimate user-facing function and is solely intended for unauthorized data collection, reconnaissance, and exfiltration, representing a clear infostealer threat.

attack_chain.action: User is lured into opening a ZIP archive containing a file with a double extension (e.g., .pdf.exe or .xls.exe), disguised as a document with a document icon and Russian-language filename.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of the malicious infostealer executable

attack_chain.action: Malicious executable runs and collects system, user, hardware, and network information from the victim's machine using multiple data collection routines.
attack_chain.leads_to: Preparation of collected data for exfiltration

attack_chain.action: Collected data is optionally encoded (e.g., hexadecimal) for obfuscation prior to transmission.
attack_chain.leads_to: Obfuscated data ready for exfiltration

attack_chain.action: Data is exfiltrated to a hardcoded C2 server or, in some variants, to an internal IP address for testing or evasion.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives victim data for reconnaissance, profiling, or future attacks

behavioral_signatures: Execution of files with double extensions (e.g., .pdf.exe, .xls.exe) masquerading as documents and using document icons
Enumeration of system, hardware, user, and network information immediately after execution of the dropped executable
Outbound HTTP POST requests to hardcoded C2 domains or internal IPs with collected system data in the request body
Use of custom HTTP headers (e.g., Cookie: 3rd_eye=<hash>) for victim identification during exfiltration
Encoding (e.g., hexadecimal) of exfiltrated data prior to transmission to C2 endpoints
file_indicators: Files with double extensions (e.g., .pdf.exe, .xls.exe) in user download or temporary directories
Dropped executables with Russian-language filenames (e.g., 'Табель учета рабочего времени.xls.exe', 'CMK Правила оформления больничных листов.pdf.exe')
Presence of executables with document icons masquerading as legitimate documents
network_indicators: HTTP POST requests to domains: shlalala.ru, ohmycars.ru, anime-clab.ru, glovatickets.ru (all using /ch3ckState or /general/ch3ckState endpoints)
HTTP POST requests to internal IPs (e.g., 10.10.30.36, 192.168.21.182) on /ch3ckState endpoint
Custom HTTP header: Cookie: 3rd_eye=<hash> used in outbound requests
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for execution of files with double extensions and document icons, especially those originating from ZIP archives and with Russian-language filenames. Detect processes that enumerate system, hardware, and user information immediately after launch. Inspect outbound HTTP POST requests to known C2 domains (shlalala.ru, ohmycars.ru, anime-clab.ru, glovatickets.ru) or internal IPs, particularly those containing system inventory data or using custom headers like '3rd_eye'. Flag exfiltration attempts where data is encoded (e.g., hexadecimal) prior to transmission. Correlate these behaviors to identify infostealer activity and prevent unauthorized data exfiltration.

package_info.why_malicious: BOLDMOVE is a custom backdoor malware family deployed via exploitation of the FortiOS/FortiProxy SSL-VPN vulnerability (CVE-2022-42475). It enables remote code execution, persistent unauthorized access, system reconnaissance, and command-and-control operations, posing a severe threat to affected systems.

attack_chain.action: Attacker exploits CVE-2022-42475 vulnerability in FortiOS/FortiProxy SSL-VPN to gain code execution.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malware deployment

attack_chain.action: BOLDMOVE malware is deployed and executed on the compromised system.
attack_chain.leads_to: Backdoor operation

attack_chain.action: Malware establishes a command-and-control channel, collects host information, and exfiltrates it to the attacker.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains situational awareness

attack_chain.action: Malware executes arbitrary commands received from the attacker and establishes persistence mechanisms.
attack_chain.leads_to: Long-term unauthorized access and control

behavioral_signatures: Unusual outbound network connections from FortiOS/FortiProxy devices to external IPs/domains not associated with legitimate Fortinet services
Execution of unknown or unsigned binaries on FortiOS/FortiProxy systems following exploitation attempts
Automated collection and exfiltration of host system information (e.g., hostname, OS version, process list) to remote servers
Unauthorized creation or modification of system startup entries or scheduled tasks by non-standard binaries
file_indicators: Presence of binaries matching known BOLDMOVE hashes (e.g., 12e28c14bb7f7b9513a02e5857592ad7, 3191cb2e06e9a30792309813793f78b6, etc.)
Unexpected files or executables in system startup locations (e.g., Windows registry Run keys, scheduled tasks, /etc/init.d/ on Linux)
Binaries with anomalous file names or locations not matching standard Fortinet software
network_indicators: Outbound connections from FortiOS/FortiProxy devices to attacker-controlled C2 infrastructure (IPs/domains as listed in threat intelligence feeds)
Exfiltration of system information over non-standard ports or protocols (e.g., custom TCP/UDP ports not used by Fortinet services)
C2 traffic patterns such as periodic beaconing or command-response sessions
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for exploitation attempts against CVE-2022-42475, unexpected execution of unknown binaries on FortiOS/FortiProxy devices, and outbound connections to unrecognized IPs or domains. Use file integrity monitoring to detect the presence of files matching known BOLDMOVE hashes and unauthorized changes to system startup settings or scheduled tasks. Analyze network traffic for exfiltration of system information and C2 communication patterns. Correlate these indicators to identify and respond to BOLDMOVE infections.
